clue.text: Pirate's leader aware of refusal to turn back boat

indicators.note: a pirate's leader is the first letter of the word Pirate's

parts.note: to be onto something is to be aware of it

indicators.note: asks for the word for refusal to be read backwards

parts.note: no is a refusal

explanation.surface: A pirate captain who knows his men refuse to retreat sends the boat back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to turn back' makes ON from NO.
explanation.definitionFit: A pontoon is a flat-bottomed boat, often used to support a floating bridge.

clue.text: Correct urge to capture province

indicators.note: the urge word grabs and holds the province letters inside

parts.note: to push is to urge
NI is Northern Ireland, often called the Province

explanation.surface: A rightful urge to seize a province.
explanation.definitionFit: Correct is used as a verb meaning to discipline, as in correcting a child.

clue.text: Recent demand for course

parts.note: new means recent
a market for something is the demand for it

explanation.surface: Recent demand for a training course.
explanation.walkthrough: Newmarket is a horse-racing town in Suffolk, England, and also a card game.
explanation.definitionFit: Newmarket is a famous racecourse, and a course is a place for horse racing.

clue.text: Doctor into rock as solo player

indicators.note: the doctor letters go inside the rock word

parts.note: ore is rock containing metal
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A doctor heading out to rock climb on his own.
explanation.definitionFit: In the card game ombre, the ombre is the player who plays alone against the other two.

clue.text: Corrupt banks earn from American state

indicators.note: corrupt means spoiled or perverted, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Crooked banks profit from an American state.
explanation.definitionFit: A Nebraskan is a person or thing from Nebraska, a state in the US Midwest.

clue.text: Hidden danger behind returning medication boxes

indicators.note: the medication word encloses the other piece, as a box holds its contents

parts.note: a pill is a dose of medication

indicators.note: the word for behind is read backwards

parts.note: aft means at the back, behind, on a ship

explanation.surface: Danger lurks in what boxes of pills hide when they come back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'behind' looks like a preposition, but it is the word to replace with its nautical synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: A pitfall is literally a concealed pit trap, and figuratively any unsuspected hazard.

clue.text: Set step across line

indicators.note: the step word stretches across the line letter, enclosing it

parts.note: a pace is a step

explanation.surface: An instruction to step over a line.
explanation.definitionFit: To place something is to set it down in position.

clue.text: Seizes day to commit to alliance

parts.note: takes means seizes
the ides was a particular day in the Roman calendar, the middle of the month

explanation.surface: One seizes the day to pledge loyalty to an alliance.
explanation.definitionFit: To take sides is to align oneself with one party in a dispute.

clue.text: Saw commercial over time

indicators.note: in a down entry the commercial word sits above the time word

parts.note: an ad is a commercial
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Watching a commercial overrun its time slot.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old saying or proverb.

clue.text: Promising characteristic of heartless lady

parts.note: 'that's just like him' means characteristic of him

indicators.note: the middle of lady is removed, leaving its outer letters

explanation.surface: A cold-hearted lady with a promising trait.
explanation.definitionFit: A likely candidate is a promising one, probable to succeed.

clue.text: Prince from West Africa wearing collar

indicators.note: the letters for West Africa sit inside the collar word as if dressed in it

parts.note: to collar a criminal is to nab them
A is a standard abbreviation for Africa

explanation.surface: A West African prince is pictured in a fine collar.
explanation.definitionFit: A nawab was a Muslim ruler or governor in Mughal India, a princely title.

clue.text: Need bit of joist in support for flag

indicators.note: the need and joist pieces go inside the support word

parts.note: to back someone is to support them
lack means need

indicators.note: only the first letter of joist is taken

explanation.surface: A flagpole needs a joist for support.
explanation.walkthrough: The blackjack was the pirates' black flag, and also the card game pontoon's cousin.
explanation.definitionFit: Blackjack is a name for the pirate flag, the Jolly Roger.

clue.text: Impasse as bay abandons horse from the same yard

indicators.note: the bay letter leaves the stable companion word, so it is deleted

parts.note: a stablemate is a horse trained at the same stable or yard
B is the racing abbreviation for a bay horse in form books

explanation.surface: A bay horse leaves its yard companion, leaving a stuck situation.
explanation.definitionFit: Stalemate is a chess position with no legal move, hence any deadlock.

clue.text: Over time plug bargain

indicators.note: the plug word goes over the time letter, holding it inside

parts.note: a seal plugs an opening

explanation.surface: Plugging a product over time gets you a bargain.
explanation.definitionFit: Something bought very cheaply is called a steal, an informal word for a bargain.

clue.text: Dropping fish without tail

indicators.note: the final letter of the fish word is cut off

parts.note: skate is a flat fish

explanation.surface: A fish loses its tail and is dropped.
explanation.walkthrough: Skat is a German card game; its name comes from Italian scarto, a discard, and the skat is the pair of cards dropped by the declarer.
explanation.definitionFit: The skat in the card game is the set of cards discarded, so the word means a discard.

clue.text: Somehow not new, yet not of a significant age

indicators.note: somehow suggests the words are arranged in some other way

explanation.surface: Someone not new to the world, yet not of a significant age.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram uses only 'not new, yet'; the second 'not' and 'of' join it to the definition. Twenty-one is also another name for the card game pontoon.
explanation.definitionFit: Twenty-one was the traditional age of coming of age, celebrated as a milestone birthday.

clue.text: King left donkey going around rich source of wealth

parts.note: K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

indicators.note: the donkey wanders about, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A king and a donkey travel around in search of riches.
explanation.definitionFit: The Klondike gold rush in Canada made the name a byword for a source of great riches.

clue.text: Performed better in unpopular drama before journalist

indicators.note: the drama word comes before the journalist letters

parts.note: out means out of fashion, unpopular
a play is a drama
ED, editor, is the usual crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A journalist reviews a better performance in an unpopular drama.
explanation.definitionFit: To outplay an opponent is to perform better than them in a game.

clue.text: Roguishly and grandly removing hat following king and knight

indicators.note: the trimmed grandly word comes after king and knight

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
N is the chess abbreviation for knight

indicators.note: the first letter, the hat on top, is taken off the grandly word

parts.note: lavishly means grandly, with great expense

explanation.surface: A grand figure takes off his hat to follow a king and a knight.
explanation.definitionFit: A knave is a rogue, so behaving knavishly is behaving like a rogue.

clue.text: Networking system using alien trap to snare female

indicators.note: the female word is caught between the alien and trap pieces

parts.note: ET is the film's extraterrestrial
a net is a trap
her is a female pronoun

explanation.surface: An alien sets a trap to catch a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethernet is the standard technology for wired local-area computer networks.

clue.text: Turning slates for photograph

indicators.note: the word for slates is turned round, read backwards

parts.note: to slate and to pan both mean to criticise harshly

explanation.surface: Roof slates are turned over for a photograph.
explanation.definitionFit: A snap is a snapshot, a quick informal photo.

clue.text: Sieves covering Welsh birds

indicators.note: the sieves word wraps round the Welsh letter

parts.note: to sieve flour is to sift it

explanation.surface: Sieves draped over Welsh birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Swifts are fast-flying birds with long scythe-shaped wings.

clue.text: Maintained time's over

parts.note: something over has ended

explanation.surface: The announcement that time has run out.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'time's' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To tend a garden is to look after or maintain it.

clue.text: Silence wife and husband first

parts.note: first written as 1ST, with the 1 as the letter I

explanation.surface: A wife wants silence, and wants her husband to go first.
explanation.walkthrough: 1ST becomes IST by reading the numeral 1 as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Whist is an old call for quiet, like hush, and can mean to be silent.

clue.text: One doing very little in bridle-roads

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the letters of bridle-roads

explanation.surface: Someone loafing about on bridle roads.
explanation.definitionFit: An idler is a lazy person who does as little work as possible.

clue.text: Small diamonds dropped from editorial about diamond

indicators.note: the remaining letters are moved about into a new order
the diamonds letter is taken out of the editorial word

parts.note: D is the card abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: An editorial about a small diamond that dropped its other stones.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing D leaves EITORIAL, rearranged ('about') as OLITAIRE.
explanation.definitionFit: A solitaire is a single gemstone, typically a diamond, set alone in a ring.

clue.text: Plans of small particles broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means spoken out on air, so the word for small particles is said aloud

parts.note: specks are small particles

explanation.surface: Plans for small particles to be scattered.
explanation.definitionFit: Specs, short for specifications, are detailed design plans.

clue.text: At first you decided awful outfit turned up is flattering one

indicators.note: in a down entry the picked letters are read from the bottom upwards
the first letters of the five following words are picked

explanation.surface: You decided the awful outfit someone turned up in was flattering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At first' takes initials through 'turned', giving YDAOT; 'up' then reverses them.
explanation.definitionFit: A toady is a sycophant who flatters to win favour.

clue.text: Excessively and completely overwhelming several

indicators.note: the completely word surrounds and swamps the word for several

parts.note: fully means completely
some means several

explanation.surface: Praise piled on so thickly that it overwhelms several people.
explanation.definitionFit: Fulsomely means in an overdone, cloying way, to excess.

clue.text: Pest concealed by a piano

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
hid means concealed

explanation.surface: A pest hides under a piano.
explanation.definitionFit: Aphids are sap-sucking insects, a common garden pest.

clue.text: Cryptic setter's ways

indicators.note: cryptic means puzzling or obscured, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: The ways of a cryptic crossword setter.
explanation.definitionFit: Streets are roads, and 'way' is common in street names.

clue.text: Unemotional doctor looked on after final bit of surgery

indicators.note: the looked-on word comes after the last letter of surgery
only the last letter of surgery is taken

parts.note: to eye something is to look at it, so looked gives eyed

explanation.surface: A doctor watches calmly after the end of an operation.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone dry-eyed sheds no tears, so shows no emotion.
